title: Interviewer Rotation Capacity Matrix and Labor‑Led Tuning Guide
body:
Purpose:
This working note defines a lightweight, repeatable approach to sizing interviewer capacity, rotating interviewers across hiring lanes, and running periodic labor‑led tuning sessions. The goal is to keep candidate experience consistent, reduce interviewer burnout, and make assignment decisions defensible when demand spikes.

Scope and audience:
- People Ops (global) and Hiring Managers
- Recruiting coordinators and interview enablement leads
- Interview panel owners in Eng/Product/SRE/Platform

Why this exists (short):
We see uneven interviewer utilization across teams (some interviewers doing 6+ screens/week; others <1). That causes quality drift, scheduling friction, and long time‑to‑offer. We need a practical matrix and a small set of operational rituals to balance load without creating heavy process overhead.

Core concepts (quick):
- Interviewer Capacity Unit (ICU): a single 45–60m technical screen counts as 1 ICU; short behavioral screen is 0.5 ICU; take-home grading session = 0.75 ICU.
- Lane: a hiring focus (e.g., backend-engineer, infra-sre, frontend, data-platform).
- Commitment window: rolling 4‑week period for measuring utilization and scheduling rotations.

How to build the matrix (step-by-step):
1) Inventory active interviewers: name, lane(s) they staff, preferred timeblocks, timezone, hiring level comfort (IC1–IC5), and weekly max ICU capacity (manager signed).
2) Pull the last 8 weeks of scheduled interviews (calendar export + ATS) to compute average weekly ICU per interviewer and per lane.
3) Compute target utilization: aim for 25–45% utilization (i.e., an interviewer who can do 6 ICUs/week should be scheduled for ~1.5–2.7 ICUs/week average). This preserves ramp, incident duty, and deep work.
4) Derive lane supply/demand: for each lane, sum available ICU capacity from interviewers mapped to the lane; compare to weekly ICU demand (incoming candidates * screens per candidate).
5) Identify delta and classify: under‑resourced lanes (supply < demand by >20%), over‑resourced lanes (>20% surplus), and balanced lanes.

Practical templates (use these in the spreadsheet or ATS tag):
- Interviewer row: name | primary lane | secondary lanes | timezone | avail blocks (Morn/Aft) | max ICU/week | avg ICU (4w) | assigned % (4w) | notes
- Lane summary row: lane | weekly demand ICU | available ICU | net delta | action (redeploy/triage/hire)

Rotation playbook (operational rituals):
- Weekly triage (15m): Recruiting + People Ops review lanes with >15% delta. Quick actions: nudge managers, reassign floating interviewers, prioritize candidates for triage.
- Labor‑Led Tuning (monthly, 60m): cross‑functional group (people‑ops recruiter, two interviewer reps, hiring manager) reviews rubric drift, average candidate pass rates, and interviewer-level calibration notes. Outcome: adjust lane assignments, recommend shadow pairs, and flag calibration training.
- Quarterly recheck: re-run the 8‑week pull; validate utilization target and re‑baseline max ICU values with managers.

Assignment heuristics (fast rules):
- New interviewers: cap at 0.6 ICU/week for the first month (shadowing counts at full weight).
- High‑impact interviews (senior IC4/IC5): prefer interviewers with recent related hiring success or explicit manager recommendation; allocate extra prep time.
- Timezone edges: for roles requiring real‑time collaboration cross‑APAC/EU/NA, prioritize interviewers whose working hours overlap at least 3 hours.

Burnout signals to watch for (automated and manual):
- >80% utilization sustained for 2+ weeks
- Increase in reschedules/cancelations per interviewer (>3x baseline)
- Drop in rubric score variance (many consistently low variance scores can mean rubber‑stamping)
- Direct feedback from interviewers via monthly pulse

Remediation playbook (if burnout flags triggered):
- Immediate: auto‑pause non‑critical interview assignments for 1 week (reassign to floats)
- Short term: pair interviewer with a junior shadow and reduce assigned ICU by 30% for 2 weeks
- Medium term: re‑calibrate expectations with manager; consider backfill or temporary external panel (contract interviewers)

Calibration and rubric tuning (labor‑led session guide):
Prework: collate 6 representative candidate writeups and scores from the last month across levels.
Agenda (60m):
- 0–10m: recap utilization metrics for lanes
- 10–30m: score a representative packet live (anonymous) and capture rubrics where raters diverge
- 30–45m: discuss scoring patterns — are certain rubric sections consistently under/overweighted?
- 45–55m: decide on one small rubric tweak and one interviewer enablement action (e.g., two short videos or a 1:1 calibration session)
- 55–60m: assign owners and timeline

Tools and minimal automation recommended:
- Simple Google Sheet (seed template attached) for the capacity matrix and per‑lane summary (columns listed above).
- Weekly calendar export automation (Zapier/Make or ATS export) to a People Ops folder for last 8 weeks.
- Slack bot that pings interviewers with weekly assigned ICU and a quick accept/decline link (reduces reschedule friction).

Operational examples (scenarios):
- Scenario A: sudden spike in infra‑SRE interviews (demand +60% week over week). Action: run weekly triage; redeploy two generalist backend interviewers for one week; escalate to hiring manager to triage candidates; open temp contract interviewer slot if spike persists >3 weeks.
- Scenario B: single interviewer has 4 reschedules in 10 days and util rate 85%. Action: auto‑pause assignments for 7 days; recruiter routes remaining candidates to floats; people ops schedules 30m check‑in.

Open questions / tradeoffs we still need to decide (for discussion):
- Exact ICU weights for pair interviews and take‑home reviews — current proposal is 0.75 but needs empirical validation across lanes.
- Whether to preserve a dedicated pool of 5% capacity as evergreen floats or make floats dynamic per quarter.
- How to integrate non‑engineering interviewers (product/design/pm) when lane demand crosses disciplines.

Immediate next steps (owner + ETA):
- Priya: publish seed Google Sheet template + import script for calendar exports (ETA 2026‑03‑09).
- Ethan: pilot weekly triage for backend and infra lanes for 4 weeks (start 2026‑03‑16).
- Lydia: recruit 4 interviewer reps for monthly tuning rotation (ETA 2026‑03‑12).

Appendix A — quick checklist for recruiters when assigning panels:
- Is the interviewer within declared max ICU capacity? (Y/N)
- Has the interviewer done a calibration session in the last 12 weeks? (Y/N)
- Is there timezone overlap of at least 2 hours for the candidate? (Y/N)
- Is the interviewer listed as a primary for this lane? If not, add to notes with reason.

Appendix B — suggested tags to add in ATS for automation:
- "ICU_primary:backend" "ICU_secondary:infra" "ICU_max:3" "ICU_pref:morn"

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a small reward (swag / recognition) for highest quality interviewer per quarter (not based on volume but candidate feedback quality).
- Experiment: let interviewers set one "focus week" per quarter where they accept no panels (deep work window) and measure impact on throughput.

This doc is a living working draft. Comments welcome in‑line and ping me in slack for quick syncs.
